explain.say: A nutcracker is two arms joined by a hinge at one end. The hinge is the pivot, the nut is the load, and your squeeze at the handle ends is the effort.

explain.say: Your hand is far from the hinge and the nut is close, so the squeeze is multiplied. Put the nut nearer the hinge and it cracks more easily, though your hands must move further.

faq.q: Where is the pivot of a nutcracker?
faq.a: The pivot is the hinge at the end where the two arms join. Both arms turn about it as you squeeze.
asks: What is the fulcrum of a nutcracker?

faq.q: Why put the nut close to the hinge?
faq.a: The closer the nut is to the hinge, compared with your hand, the more your squeeze is multiplied. A nut a fifth of the way along gets about five times your force.
asks: Where should the nut go in a nutcracker?

faq.q: What type of lever is a nutcracker?
faq.a: It is a second-class lever: the load, the nut, sits between the pivot and the effort. Wheelbarrows, bottle openers and oars are also second-class levers.
asks: Is a nutcracker a second class lever?

faq.q: How is a nutcracker like a wheelbarrow?
faq.a: In both, the pivot is at one end, the load is in the middle, and you lift or push at the far end. So both multiply your force.
asks: What other levers are like a nutcracker?

faq.q: Do second-class levers always multiply force?
faq.a: Yes. Because the effort is always further from the pivot than the load, a second-class lever always gives more force than you put in, at the cost of moving further.
asks: Why do second class levers make things easier?

facts: In a second-class lever the load is between the pivot and the effort.
Wheelbarrows and bottle openers are second-class levers like a nutcracker.

quiz.say: In a nutcracker, what lies between the hinge and your hand?
quiz.show: In a nutcracker, what lies between the hinge and your hand?
quiz.why: The nut, the load, is in the middle, which makes it a second-class lever.

wrong.1: The nut sits between the hinge and your hand.
wrong.2: There is only one hinge, at the end.

quiz.say: Which of these is also a second-class lever?
quiz.show: Which of these is also a second-class lever?
quiz.why: A wheelbarrow has its pivot, the wheel, at one end, the load in the middle and your lift at the far end.

wrong.1: Tweezers are third-class: the effort is in the middle.
wrong.2: A seesaw is first-class: the pivot is in the middle.
